title: Completion fences qualify bounded MACA captures but a later cohort still fails timing quality
observation: The two original SDK-default captures each contain a256ns same-stream overlap, at sample-to-reset and reset-to-sample boundaries. Both retained records still refuse under the successor. Host completion fences outside the measured kernel interval pass32 fresh A/A comparisons across short/medium/long kernels and serial/three-host-submission conditions, four known positive/negative paired controls, and four separate profiles. The fixed eight-combination experiment then obtains six quality-passed comparisons, all slower than the N4 whole-K strong seed. Its seventh comparison passes correctness but one baseline cohort has CV0.1767329199624791 against0.05, with minimum0.770us and median4.608us. That receipt is not a performance result. The predeclared first-invalid-quality stop prevents the remaining41 comparisons; no rejected sample is removed and no comparison is retried. No interval overlap was observed in these successor captures. The SDK mapping cause, the short baseline sample's cause, global timing reliability and interaction/generalization effects remain unestablished.
proposed_change: Retain the completion-fenced acquisition as a bounded qualified successor while keeping SDK-default timestamps, reset/stream/correlation and quality checks. Investigate the retained baseline outlier before another formal batch; do not add a duration floor, discard a sample, relax CV or retrospectively change the stop rule. Preserve F-2026-10-04-001's separate monotonic-clock limitation.

promotion_disposition: No Compiler optimization promotion. Completion-boundary source change has bounded device evidence; the broader timing-reliability finding remains deferred. Preserve all old Runs and the successor's negative and failed observations.
